topic: FSRU sub-chartered to Jordan amid indefinite Stade delay; vessel renamed Energos Force
wiki_text: The FSRU assigned to the Stade terminal — built 2021, 174,000 cbm — was originally named Transgas Force and chartered from Greece's Dynagas under a 2023 contract with the German federal economics ministry (BMWK, now BMWE). In January 2024, Energos Infrastructure, a US LNG joint venture majority-controlled by Apollo-managed funds with New Fortress Energy as minority shareholder, acquired this unit and its sister (Transgas Power) from Dynagas affiliates and renamed them Energos Force and Energos Power. The vessel arrived at Stade's AVG jetty in March 2024, but the terminal's launch was delayed indefinitely. In March 2025 DET (Deutsche Energy Terminal, the federal operator) terminated its contract with onshore developer Hanseatic Energy Hub; under a November 14 agreement DET took over the terminal superstructure to complete it, with operation not expected before Q2 2026. To avoid further financial losses during the delay, BMWE and DET sub-chartered the Energos Force to Jordan, where it is deployed to import LNG (via Egypt) until Jordan's onshore Aqaba regasification terminal is ready around end-2026.
